RUP_TRACE.construction: trace supplied; no universal finder claimed

located_bottleneck.name: CERTIFICATE_DISCOVERY_COMPLEXITY
located_bottleneck.definition: Total work to choose a proof language, discover the relevant merge certificate or canonical form, and verify it.

exact_split.canonical_P_classes: 2-SAT and GF(2) provide polynomial construction and verification.
exact_split.bounded_proof_search: Width-w Resolution is polynomial only under a fixed width bound.
exact_split.trace_verification_without_search: RUP gives polynomial replay but no universal polynomial finder.

positive_result: Four different exponential presentation artifacts were removed by independently replayable certificates without a semantic equivalence oracle.
negative_results: Blocked equality keeps 2^n continuation-distinct states under complete 2-SAT closure.
Fixed-width Resolution stays polynomial only for fixed width.
RUP verification is polynomial in a supplied trace, while unrestricted candidate search has 3^n-1 clauses.
General residual equivalence still contains UNSAT through F equivalent to FALSE.

what_improved: The merge-proof barrier is split into four executable certificate regimes.
Three certificate systems strictly stronger than subsumption collapse new exponential fake-state families.
Verification complexity and certificate-discovery complexity are separately charged.
distance_to_p_equals_np.next_exact_target: Find an instance-specific certificate selector/finder with polynomial total discovery cost that avoids unbounded Resolution width and unrestricted RUP clause search.

criterion.name: Certificate Portfolio Criterion
criterion.statement: If every necessary residual merge of every CNF has a polynomial-size certificate whose language and certificate are both discoverable and verifiable in polynomial total work, and certified residual state volume is polynomial, then SAT is in P.

claim_boundary: C026 does not prove P=NP, P!=NP, NP=coNP, or an unrestricted lower bound.
